summary: T-0741 started sending KC firstName/lastName (derived from display_name via splitDisplayName). Keycloak's declarative user-profile validates both with person-name-prohibited-characters (realm-choros.json) — a display_name with characters that validator rejects (e.g. 'Bot #1', 'A&B') now ALSO 400s from POST /admin/realms/choros/users, but createHumanUser's 400-branch (admin-port.ts) unconditionally mapped EVERY 400 to EMAIL_INVALID (correct pre-T-0741, when that was the only possible 400 cause). user-mgmt.ts then told the owner 'email must be a valid email address' for a perfectly valid email while never naming the real problem (the display name). Fix: admin-port.ts now parses the KC 400 body's field-level messageKey (extractKcFieldErrors + isPersonNameCharacterError, both LIVE-CONFIRMED against a real KC 25.0.6) and throws a new NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS code specifically when firstName/lastName fail the person-name validator; every other 400 (genuine bad email, unparseable body, unrelated-field drift) falls through UNCHANGED to EMAIL_INVALID. user-mgmt.ts maps the new code to an honest Russian 400 message; web/src/screens/users-form.js's mapUserError anchors it on the 'Отображаемое имя' field (screen-users.jsx's pre-existing generic field-anchor mechanism — no JSX changes needed).
root_cause: admin-port.ts's createHumanUser 400-branch trusted the HTTP STATUS alone (400) as sufficient to identify EMAIL_INVALID, never inspecting KC's response BODY to see which field actually failed. That was a safe simplification before T-0741 (the only 400 this endpoint could produce was error-invalid-email); T-0741 added a second class of 400 (person-name validator on firstName/lastName) through the SAME status code, and the old branch silently absorbed it under the old label — a misattributed error, not a missing one.
live_proof: docs/tasks/T-0748.spec.md §3 — real KC 25.0.6 (container t-0633-keycloak-1, :8180, choros-registrar client_credentials, the EXACT path createHumanUser itself uses), probed 2026-07-11. Confirmed the two live 400 body shapes admin-port.ts now parses: single-object {field,errorMessage} when one field fails, {errors:[...]} array when multiple fail in the same request. Person-name validator's messageKey is 'error-person-name-invalid-character', always on field firstName/lastName, never on email. No orphan KC users left behind by any 400 case (KC rolls the create back on validation failure — verified by re-querying all 4 throwaway probe usernames post-hoc: none existed). The unit tests in src/__tests__/admin-port.test.ts (AP-9) replay these exact live-observed body shapes through a local stub HTTP server — matches this file's own existing convention (AP-6/AP-8 already stub KC's 409 disambiguation the same way); the live probe is what anchors those stub bodies to reality.

Restored the fix via git apply; all 30/30 admin-port.test.ts tests green again (verified, not assumed).

security_notes: No new attack surface: this is purely an error-message ATTRIBUTION fix. The underlying create-user authorization gate (authorizeOrgWrite/loadAdminContext/assertOrgObjectAuthority) and the anti-collision LOGIN_RESERVED guard are untouched (diff starts strictly after kc.createHumanUser's catch block).

extractKcFieldErrors/isPersonNameCharacterError only ever READ Keycloak's own response body to pick a more specific error CODE — no new trust boundary crossed, no new external input accepted (the body already flows through this function's neighbor extractKcErrorMessage for the 409 case since T-0633).

Safe-default preserved end-to-end: any 400 body shape this parser doesn't recognize (empty, unparseable, unrelated field, KC-version drift) falls through to the EXACT prior EMAIL_INVALID behavior — proven by 3 explicit regression tests at the admin-port.ts layer and 1 at the user-mgmt.ts/DB layer.
follow_ups: Not fixed here (T-0741 §6, unchanged, out of scope): src/core/register.ts (self-registration) does not pass displayName to createHumanUser at all, so this class of error cannot occur on that path — but self-registration also cannot yet benefit from T-0741's firstName/lastName fix either (its display_name is the email address, splitting it would be nonsense). Pre-existing gap, not introduced or widened by T-0748.
judge_attack_surface: Try a KC 400 that has BOTH a bad email AND a bad name in the same request ({errors:[...]} array) — must still surface NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS, not silently prefer the email branch (AP-9 case 3, DB test not separately covering the mixed case — only the unit layer does, since the DB test drives the fake port which models one KC-side code at a time, not raw KC body parsing).

Try to break the substring match in isPersonNameCharacterError with a field that happens to contain 'person-name' in its NAME but isn't firstName/lastName — the field check (fe.field === 'firstName' || fe.field === 'lastName') is a hard equality gate BEFORE the substring check, so this cannot false-positive on e.g. a hypothetical 'personNameHint' field.
Try an ordinary two-word Cyrillic display_name end-to-end through the real HTTP route (DB test 'T-0748 regression: an ordinary display_name...') — must still 201, unaffected.

Try the KC-side EMAIL_INVALID path (DB test 'T-0748 regression: KC-side EMAIL_INVALID...') via a monkey-patched kc.createHumanUser — must produce the BYTE-IDENTICAL prior message 'email must be a valid email address (e.g. name@company.ru)', not the new Russian name message.

Try mounting the real CreateUserModal and submitting with a NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS response — must show the message anchored on Отображаемое имя (aria-invalid=true) and NOT on Email; the pre-fix misleading email text must be entirely absent from the dialog (screen-users.mount.test.jsx).
